sentences.en: I'm Vivian Le, in this week for Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是薇薇安·勒，本周代班罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: I was raised in a Vietnamese household, which means I was practically born with a karaoke mic in my hand.
sentences.zh: 我在越南家庭长大，这意味着我几乎是手里拿着卡拉OK麦克风出生的。

sentences.en: Birthdays, family reunions, funerals, Sunday mornings after the Raiders lost, all good reasons to whip out the karaoke machine.
sentences.zh: 生日聚会、家庭团聚、葬礼、突袭者队输球后的周日早晨，这些都是拿出卡拉OK机的绝佳理由。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I remember most vividly during these formative mid-90s moments
sentences.zh: 在这些90年代中期的成长记忆中，我印象最深刻的事情之一

sentences.en: was watching the videos that played during the karaoke tracks my parents were singing along to.
sentences.zh: 就是看着父母跟着唱卡拉OK时屏幕上播放的视频。

sentences.en: They were mostly stock footage synchronized to the music.
sentences.zh: 它们大多是与音乐同步的素材片段。

sentences.en: You know, people on a beach, people sailing boats, people in a hot air balloon.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，海滩上的人、开帆船的人、坐热气球的人。

sentences.en: Every time I hear the song, listen to the rhythm of the falling rain,
sentences.zh: 每当我听到那首《听着雨落的节奏》，

sentences.en: I could still see freestyle roller skaters weaving through cones in an urban park.
sentences.zh: 我依然能看到自由式轮滑选手在城市公园里穿梭于路障之间。

sentences.en: These videos were like watching the equivalent of hotel art.
sentences.zh: 这些视频就像是酒店里的装饰画。

sentences.en: Something to look at, not necessarily something to think about.
sentences.zh: 只是用来看看，并不需要去思考什么。

sentences.en: In other words, they were nothing like the karaoke videos that Brian Raftery was watching when he was in his 20s.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它们和布莱恩·拉夫特里二十多岁时看的卡拉OK视频完全不同。

sentences.en: I definitely remember nights and times when I was singing when everyone would just kind of turn their head toward the video
sentences.zh: 我确实记得有那么些夜晚，当我唱歌时，大家会不约而同地转头看向视频，

sentences.en: because they were so strange and they're so ambitious and they're so weird.
sentences.zh: 因为它们太奇怪、太有野心、也太诡异了。

sentences.en: And some of them look really great.
sentences.zh: 而且其中一些看起来真的很棒。

sentences.en: Brian is a culture writer and author of the book Don't Stop Believin',
sentences.zh: 布莱恩是一位文化作家，也是《别停止相信》一书的作者，

sentences.en: How Karaoke Conquered the World and Changed My Life.
sentences.zh: 副标题是《卡拉OK如何征服世界并改变了我的人生》。

sentences.en: Brian's entry point to karaoke came in the late 1990s.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩是在90年代末接触到卡拉OK的。

sentences.en: He and his friends were living in New York City when they discovered a little dive called Village Karaoke.
sentences.zh: 当时他和朋友住在纽约市，发现了一家叫“乡村卡拉OK”的小酒吧。

sentences.en: It was during these late night excursions that he realized the karaoke videos playing at Village were on a whole other level.
sentences.zh: 正是在这些深夜的消遣中，他意识到“乡村”酒吧里播放的卡拉OK视频完全是另一个档次。

sentences.en: Like the Benny and the Jets video, you can interpret that song 85 million ways.
sentences.zh: 就像《本尼与喷气机》那首歌，你可以有8500万种解读方式。

sentences.en: But the video we remembered, for some reason, was like a mom luring a bunch of kids slowly to a plate full of cookies.
sentences.zh: 但我们记得的那个视频，不知为何，拍的是一位妈妈慢慢地把一群孩子引向一盘饼干。

sentences.en: And I'm like, what the hell does this have to do with Benny and the Jets?
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，这到底和《本尼与喷气机》有什么关系？
既没有本尼，也没有喷气机。

sentences.en: It wasn't like these videos were unrelated stock footage just thrown over music.
sentences.zh: 这些视频可不是随便套在音乐上的无关素材。

sentences.en: These are all originally produced short films, equipped with their own storylines, characters, and tangential interpretations of the song's lyrics.
sentences.zh: 它们都是原创的短片，有自己的故事情节、角色，以及对歌词的侧面解读。

sentences.en: And there are literally thousands of videos like this.
sentences.zh: 这样的视频足有成千上万个。

sentences.en: There's a very strange video that we used to talk about all the time for Paul McCartney's Ebony and Ivory,
sentences.zh: 有一个我们以前经常谈论的非常奇怪的视频，是保罗·麦卡特尼的《乌木与象牙》，

sentences.en: which was really, I don't know if it's problematic or not, but it was like,
sentences.zh: 我不知道这算不算有问题，但内容是这样的：

sentences.en: there's a black man walking a white dog and then a white man walking a black dog.
sentences.zh: 一个黑人牵着一只白狗，然后一个白人牵着一只黑狗。

sentences.en: It is trying to be true to the spirit of this, you know, Paul McCartney, Stevie Wonder duet.
sentences.zh: 它试图忠实于保罗·麦卡特尼和史蒂夫·汪达这首二重唱的精神内核。

sentences.en: But it makes no sense that it's a dog park.
sentences.zh: 但把场景设在狗公园里实在让人摸不着头脑。

sentences.en: Some of these karaoke videos were clearly bananas, but they were not lacking in ambition.
sentences.zh: 有些卡拉OK视频显然疯得离谱，但它们并不缺乏野心。

sentences.en: Actors were hired, locations were scouted, lighting was designed, and a lot of them were shot on actual film stock.
sentences.zh: 他们雇佣演员、勘景、设计灯光，很多视频还是用真正的胶片拍摄的。

sentences.en: Ryan wanted to know who had made these and why go through all the effort.
sentences.zh: 瑞安想知道是谁制作了这些视频，为什么要费这么大劲。

sentences.en: I was just kind of like, this is weird that like, this is a video that like,
sentences.zh: 我当时就觉得，这太奇怪了，我们只是为了好玩才来这儿，

sentences.en: we're just here as a goof and someone put a lot of time and effort to make this video for this Hall & Oates song that we're all drunkenly singing in a tiny room.
sentences.zh: 而有人却投入了大量的时间和精力，为我们这群在狭小房间里醉醺醺唱着的霍尔与奥兹乐队的歌制作了视频。

sentences.en: As it turns out, these weirdo karaoke videos were kind of their own micro movement of filmmaking.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这些古怪的卡拉OK视频本身就是一种微型的电影运动。

sentences.en: It only lasted a handful of years and is only remembered by a handful of people, but it gave a generation of aspiring filmmakers something that barely exists anymore.
sentences.zh: 它只持续了短短几年，也只有少数人记得，但它为一代有抱负的电影人提供了一种现在几乎不存在的东西。

sentences.en: A paying gig where they could just mess around and figure out how to make stuff.
sentences.zh: 一份能让他们随意折腾、摸索制作门道的带薪工作。

sentences.en: It's about as close to an outside of Hollywood, Hollywood project as you can get.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就是你能接触到的最接近好莱坞之外的好莱坞项目了。

sentences.en: Some videos were good, some were bad, and several were so bad that they were awesome.
sentences.zh: 有些视频很好，有些很烂，还有一些烂到极致反而成了经典。

sentences.en: And I had to know more about where they came from.
sentences.zh: 我必须弄清楚它们到底从何而来。

sentences.en: The story of these videos actually originated about a decade before Brian discovered them at Village Karaoke.
sentences.zh: 这些视频的故事实际上起源于布莱恩在“乡村卡拉OK”发现它们的大约十年前。

sentences.en: Back in the 1980s, the world of consumer electronics was exploding.
sentences.zh: 回到80年代，消费电子产品领域正在爆发。

sentences.en: Personal computers, the Walkman, camcorders, fax machines, the Game Boy.
sentences.zh: 个人电脑、随身听、摄像机、传真机、Game Boy。

sentences.en: It was like a shiny new toy was coming out on a monthly basis.
sentences.zh: 就像每个月都有闪亮的新玩具问世一样。
尼尔·奥特纽也想分一杯羹。

sentences.en: I basically was a sales and marketing exec, and I introduced a lot of products to the United States.
sentences.zh: 我当时基本上是一名销售和营销主管，我向美国引进了许多产品。

sentences.en: One day in 1988, Neil was flipping through the New York Times, and he saw a job ad that intrigued him.
sentences.zh: 1988年的一天，尼尔在翻阅《纽约时报》时，看到了一则让他感兴趣的招聘广告。

sentences.en: And they were looking for somebody, for some sort of a startup in the East CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们正在东海岸为某种初创公司寻找人才。

sentences.en: The company that put out that ad was Pioneer, the Japanese Electronics Corporation.
sentences.zh: 发布那则广告的公司是日本电子巨头先锋公司。

sentences.en: They were looking for someone to head up a brand new division, specifically in America.
sentences.zh: 他们正在寻找一位负责人，专门负责美国的一个全新部门。

sentences.en: Neil applied, and when he got an interview, his wife drove down with him to the Pioneer offices in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 尼尔申请了职位，面试时，他的妻子开车陪他去了曼哈顿的先锋办公室。

sentences.en: Well, you know, maybe two hours passed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，大概过了两个小时。

sentences.en: I came down and I said, this is a really interesting product.
sentences.zh: 我走下来，说，这是一个非常有趣的产品。

sentences.en: And she said, what is it?
And I said, it's this thing called karaoke.
Karaoke had been around for over a decade at this point.
sentences.zh: 当时卡拉OK已经存在十多年了。

sentences.en: But back in the 1980s, it was still pretty unknown in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 但在80年代，它在西方仍然鲜为人知。

sentences.en: It was huge in Asia, though, particularly in Japan, where Pioneer was headquartered.
sentences.zh: 不过它在亚洲非常火，特别是在先锋总部所在的日本。

sentences.en: The word karaoke itself is Japanese, meaning empty orchestra.
sentences.zh: “卡拉OK”这个词本身就是日语，意思是“空管弦乐”。

sentences.en: If you go to Japan, every little bar, there was 800,000 bars in Japan, believe it or not.
sentences.zh: 如果你去日本，每个小酒吧——信不信由你，日本有80万家酒吧——

sentences.en: But every bar had to have karaoke in it.
sentences.zh: 每个酒吧都必须有卡拉OK。

sentences.en: And actually, a big reason why karaoke was already so popular in Japan was because of Pioneer's karaoke technology.
sentences.zh: 事实上，卡拉OK在日本之所以如此流行，很大程度上归功于先锋的卡拉OK技术。

sentences.en: A few years before Neil joined the company, Pioneer completely revolutionized the karaoke game by releasing the first ever karaoke laser disc player.
sentences.zh: 在尼尔加入公司前几年，先锋通过发布史上第一台卡拉OK激光视盘机，彻底改变了卡拉OK的游戏规则。

sentences.en: For those under the age of 37, LaserDisc was one of the lesser-known combatants in the home video format wars of the 70s and 80s.
sentences.zh: 对于37岁以下的人来说，激光视盘是70和80年代家庭视频格式大战中不太出名的一员。

sentences.en: Picture a DVD the size of a vinyl record.
sentences.zh: 想象一下一张黑胶唱片大小的DVD。

sentences.en: And I've got one on my hand right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在手里就拿着一张。

sentences.en: And it has information on both sides.
Okay, and there's 28 videos on each disc.
sentences.zh: 好了，每张盘上有28个视频。

sentences.en: Back then, when home video was first emerging,
sentences.zh: 那时候，当家庭视频刚开始出现时，

sentences.en: VHS, Betamax, and LaserDisc were all battling it out to be the dominant consumer technology.
sentences.zh: VHS、Betamax和激光视盘都在争夺消费技术的主导地位。

sentences.en: VHS and Beta turned out to be exponentially more popular for the home movie watching experience.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，VHS和Beta在家庭电影观看体验上要普及得多。
录像带赢得了那场战争。

sentences.en: LaserDisc only was able to capture maybe 1% of the market.
sentences.zh: 激光视盘只占领了大约1%的市场份额。

sentences.en: But the video market is so huge, 1% of the market is very significant.
sentences.zh: 但视频市场太大了，1%的市场份额也非常可观。

sentences.en: So Pioneer says, you know what, maybe not so much for movies, but karaoke, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以先锋说，你知道吗，电影方面可能不行，但卡拉OK，没问题。

sentences.en: Because nobody else is doing it.
sentences.zh: 因为没有别人在做这个。

sentences.en: So we'll take 1% of the market all alone.
sentences.zh: 那我们就独占这1%的市场吧。

sentences.en: When it came to something like karaoke,
sentences.zh: 当涉及到卡拉OK这类产品时，

sentences.en: LaserDisc had a superpower that gave it an edge over VHS or Beta.
sentences.zh: 激光视盘拥有一种使其优于VHS或Beta的超能力。

sentences.en: A LaserDisc could jump around to individual chapters on the disc.
sentences.zh: 激光视盘可以跳转到盘上的各个章节。

sentences.en: This made it well-suited for searching for individual karaoke tracks
sentences.zh: 这使得它非常适合搜索单首卡拉OK曲目，

sentences.en: if they were listed as chapters, like you would on a jukebox.
sentences.zh: 如果它们像点唱机那样被列为章节的话。

sentences.en: It was a technology that fit the art form.
sentences.zh: 这是一种契合这种艺术形式的技术。

sentences.en: Pioneer said, you know what, for a karaoke application, this is perfect.
sentences.zh: 先锋说，你知道吗，对于卡拉OK应用来说，这太完美了。

sentences.en: Essentially, all you need for karaoke are two things.
sentences.zh: 本质上，卡拉OK只需要两样东西。

sentences.en: A backing track and the lyrics to the song displayed on the screen.
sentences.zh: 伴奏音乐和屏幕上显示的歌词。

sentences.en: But when Pioneer manufactured these discs for the Japanese market,
sentences.zh: 但当先锋为日本市场生产这些光盘时，

sentences.en: they also decided to include one additional element.
sentences.zh: 他们还决定加入一个额外的元素。

sentences.en: A karaoke music video that went along with each track.
sentences.zh: 每首曲目都配有一个卡拉OK音乐视频。

sentences.en: I think that the original concept of using those videos in Japan
sentences.zh: 我认为在日本使用这些视频的初衷，
基本上是为了推销激光视盘。

sentences.en: LaserDiscs were known for having really good picture resolution,
sentences.zh: 激光视盘以画质清晰著称，

sentences.en: way better than its competitors, VHS or Betamax.
Pioneer in Japan figured it would be a complete waste
sentences.zh: 日本先锋公司认为，如果不把好看的视频放在屏幕上，

sentences.en: not to put a nice-looking video up on the screen.
And Neil says when Pioneer decided to expand to the American market
sentences.zh: 尼尔说，当先锋决定进军美国市场，

sentences.en: and get laser karaoke into American bars,
sentences.zh: 并将激光卡拉OK引入美国酒吧时，
他们复制了同样的模式。

sentences.en: They had a lot of success in Japan with it that way.
sentences.zh: 他们在日本用这种方式取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: And they wanted to replicate their success in the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们想在美国复制这种成功。

sentences.en: And they felt that this is the way we did it in Japan.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得这就是我们在日本的做法。

sentences.en: We got to do it in the United States the same way.
sentences.zh: 我们必须在美国也照样做。

sentences.en: But it couldn't be exactly the same.
Those videos were shot in Japan for Japanese songs,
sentences.zh: 那些视频是在日本拍摄的，针对的是日本歌曲，

sentences.en: You know, you couldn't have a song like, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不能放一首，比如，

sentences.en: I shot the sheriff with a Japanese video on it.
sentences.zh: 《我枪杀了警长》，却配上一个日本视频。

sentences.en: You had to have a production company go out there and shoot the videos.
sentences.zh: 你必须找一家制作公司去拍摄这些视频。

sentences.en: Which is how people like Nori Niven got involved.
sentences.zh: 这就是像诺里·尼文这样的人参与进来的原因。

sentences.en: I always compared it to like that scene in Conan the Barbarian
sentences.zh: 我总是把它比作《野蛮人柯南》里的那个场景，

sentences.en: where he has to push that rock in a circle for like 10 years
sentences.zh: 他必须推着那块石头绕圈走上大约10年，

sentences.en: before he becomes a grown man, you know, when he's all strong.
sentences.zh: 直到他长成一个强壮的成年人。

sentences.en: Because you shoot a million feet of film
sentences.zh: 因为你要拍摄一百万英尺的胶片，

sentences.en: and either you fail or you come out of it stronger.
sentences.zh: 要么你失败了，要么你从中变得更强大。

sentences.en: In the late 1980s, Nori was actually still in college.
sentences.zh: 80年代末，诺里其实还在上大学。

sentences.en: He'd been directing music videos for local artists
sentences.zh: 他一直在为当地艺人导演音乐录影带，

sentences.en: when the opportunity to work on these karaoke videos fell into his lap.
sentences.zh: 这时参与这些卡拉OK视频的机会从天而降。

sentences.en: Somehow I wound up on a panel for music videos at Panavision in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 不知怎么的，我最终参加了达拉斯Panavision举办的一个音乐录影带小组讨论会。

sentences.en: And one of the guys on the panel said,
hey, I've got these karaoke videos.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我手头有这些卡拉OK视频。

sentences.en: You want to come shoot some of them?
I mean, I love shooting film.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我热爱拍摄胶片。

sentences.en: And the idea of shooting music videos sounded really fun.
sentences.zh: 而且拍摄音乐录影带的想法听起来真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And of course I said yes.
Pioneer had a division called Laserdisc Corporation of America,
sentences.zh: 先锋有一个部门叫美国激光视盘公司，

sentences.en: They contracted production companies and directors
sentences.zh: 他们签约了来自洛杉矶、纽约、达拉斯甚至伦敦的制作公司和导演。

sentences.en: from Los Angeles, New York, Dallas, even London.

sentences.zh: 这些视频有一个明确的指令。

sentences.en: there was one specific directive for these videos.

sentences.zh: 我记得他们非常想要叙事感。

sentences.en: So I remember they really wanted a narrative weave.
sentences.zh: 他们想要有开头、中间和结尾。

sentences.en: They wanted a beginning, a middle, and an end.
sentences.zh: 他们真的希望你紧扣歌曲的故事情节。

sentences.en: They really wanted you to stick to the storyline of the song.
sentences.zh: 他们真的希望你紧扣歌曲的故事情节。

sentences.en: By the time Pioneer got into this,
sentences.zh: 当先锋公司介入此事时，

sentences.en: I think they needed to have some sort of story.
sentences.zh: 我想他们需要某种故事线。

sentences.en: Because at that point, Western audiences,
especially after seven or eight years of MTV,
sentences.zh: 尤其是在经历了七八年的 MTV 之后，

sentences.en: they knew that every video had to have
sentences.zh: 他们知道每支音乐录影带都必须有

sentences.en: either a wild collage or a very easy-to-follow narrative.
sentences.zh: 狂野的拼贴画面，或者非常易懂的叙事。

sentences.en: Pioneer wanted these narratives to adhere to the vibe and message of the song,
sentences.zh: 先锋公司希望这些叙事能契合歌曲的氛围和内涵，

sentences.en: but that came with one big stipulation.
sentences.zh: 但这也伴随着一个巨大的限制条件。

sentences.en: The footage used in these videos had to be completely original for copyright purposes.
sentences.zh: 出于版权考虑，这些录影带中使用的素材必须是完全原创的。
先锋公司只获得了音乐的授权，

sentences.en: not the artist's likeness or any existing music video,
sentences.zh: 并没有获得艺人的肖像权或任何现有的音乐录影带授权，

sentences.en: so you couldn't reference their vision of the song.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能参考他们对歌曲的演绎。

sentences.en: You know, if it was a song, if it was thriller,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果这是一首歌，比如《颤栗》，

sentences.en: they did not want you to do, like, the thriller dance.
sentences.zh: 他们不希望你去做那种《颤栗》的舞蹈。

sentences.en: They didn't want you to come to something original.
